grade.basis: Whole Dance No. 2 estimate, set by the upper solo-register melody in bass 1 (bass 2 also requires an experienced player). The actual Dance 2 opening establishes a moderate-pulse quasi-reggae accompaniment with pizzicato double stops; the internal mm.66–77 sample shows high treble-register melodic playing, chromatic inflections, position changes, grace notes and irregular five- and nine-note subdivisions. These call for established thumb-position intonation and rhythmic fluency, making advanced level 5 a better hardest-part fit than the publisher’s broad intermediate ensemble label. No ensemble uplift is added. Primary whole-work description explicitly places basses 1 and 2 throughout the solo register and bounds lower parts at third position with double stops. This supports an advisory whole-movement ceiling within about one level; it is not a claim to have inspected every bar. Dance 1 notation above the Dance 2 heading is excluded.

findings.finding: Publisher describes Dance 2 specifically as a reggae groove in basses 3 and 4, with melodic interest in basses 1 and 2 throughout the solo register; quoted review says the lower parts stay within third position, with double stops.
Printed page 8, lower system only: Dance No.2, Allegro con joke, dotted-quarter about 76 in 3/4; bass 4 establishes quasi-reggae pizzicato and bass 3 enters with offbeat double stops.
Printed page 13, mm.66–77: upper melodic parts, chromatic notes and ornaments, including five- and nine-note figures in bass 1; repeated offbeat accompaniment remains much simpler.

grade.basis: Whole-work advisory estimate for the standard four-bass version. Bass 1 sets the ceiling through sustained treble-register playing and the later melodic variations: mm.19–24 combine upper-register melody with eighth/sixteenth rhythms and slurred figures. Bass 2 also reaches ledger-line solo register and takes a rhythmically active theme in mm.39–42. The moderate quarter-note pulse of 86, recurring two-theme structure, mostly diatonic material, and uncomplicated lower voices keep this at early advanced level 4 rather than demanding diploma technique. Upper-register intonation, shifts, articulation and some tremolo/arco-pizzicato changes are the meaningful demands; neither massed ensemble coordination nor the optional beginner fifth part increases the grade. Opening, internal variation and later theme-transfer samples, together with the composer’s whole-work account of repeated variations, support medium confidence and roughly one-level uncertainty, not exhaustive all-bar certification.

findings.finding: Composer describes two major themes repeated in different variations and mixed-ability participation. Publisher explicitly states bass 5 is optional and first-position beginner material; the work is performable by quartet.
Opening score: Moderato quarter=86, three-sharp key signature, sustained upper bass-1 melody over accessible bass-register patterns; optional fifth staff is labeled.
Printed page 4, mm.19–26: bass 1 has active treble-register melody with sixteenth figures; bass 2 has high ledger-line writing and tremolo; lower parts remain simpler.
Printed page 6, mm.35–42: further patterned sixteenth writing, optional ad-lib fills/repeats, glissandi, and a theme transferred to bass 2. This provides variation evidence beyond the quiet opening.
